_comment: Attachments is a state process with ONE TASK PER attachment_id: the task
ref is the attachment_id, and its data is keyed by channel. Send Message
reads {{conv[<attachments_id>].ref[{{attachment_id}}].{{channel}}}}.
Create a new attachment with run-task (ref: "<attachment_id>"), update
with modify-task + deep_merge:true. A channel key that is absent means
"send no attachment on that channel" — that is legal, not an error.
Every field below is consumed by the per-channel native-syntax Code node
inside Send Message; these are the shapes it actually reads. Setting
"raw": true on a channel bypasses translation and copies your object
straight onto the channel's send payload — use it only for a shape the
template does not model.
Button labels and payloads go through the same {{var}} / {{t'key}}
interpolation as text, so a label can be a localization key. {{t'key}} has
NO dot. And {{var}} resolves against Send Message's OWN task, so the
calling command must forward that field in its api_copy data block.
REPLY KEYBOARD vs INLINE KEYBOARD decides whether a dialog can read the
answer at all. A dialog's wait node reads data.message.text. telegram
type:"keyboard" (reply keyboard) sends the button LABEL as a text
message, so the label arrives as the answer -- that is what an ask or
confirm step needs. type:"inline_keyboard" sends callback_data, which
Main -> PARSE command reads as a COMMAND, so the pending question is never
answered. Use keyboard for answer steps, inline_keyboard for menus and
display-only rows.
A DYNAMIC attachment (one carrying an items/buttons pattern) renders its
rows from the CALLING task, so the command must forward items and
currentPage on its Send Message api_copy or the carousel arrives empty.
The gate into createDynamicAttachment is `items == "" && buttons == ""`,
so a command with no rows must send items as the empty STRING: an empty
ARRAY takes the dynamic path and re-renders a static keyboard's buttons as
a per-item pattern zero times, delivering a keyboard with no buttons.
Button payload grammar (Main -> PARSE command):
"/order-status__id-42_page-2" => command /order-status, params {id:42,page:2}
separator "__", pair union "_", key/value "-". A literal - or _ inside
a value splits it, so never put free text in a payload.
Per-page item caps enforced by createDynamicAttachment:
facebook carousel 10, quick_replies 6, list 4 | viber carousel 6, keyboard 8
TELEGRAM SENDS MORE THAN KEYBOARDS. Send Message's Telegram native-syntax
node dispatches on attachment.type, and its API_Methods folder implements a
method per type -- so these are available and are NOT just keyboards.
VERIFIED ON TELEGRAM ONLY: the list below was read off the Telegram
native-syntax node and its API_Methods. Viber, Facebook and ABC have their
own native-syntax nodes with their own switch on attachment.type -- read the
one you are targeting the same way instead of assuming these names carry
over, and remember an absent channel key is legal.
{"type":"image", "url":"...", "caption":"..."}  -> sendPhoto
{"type":"video"|"audio"|"file", "url":"..."}     -> sendVideo/sendAudio/sendDocument
{"type":"location", "lat":"...", "lon":"..."}    -> sendLocation
{"type":"sticker", ...}                          -> sendSticker
url and caption go through the same {{var}} interpolation as text, so
{"type":"image","url":"{{someImageUrl}}"} renders a per-task image as long
as the command forwards someImageUrl. Omit caption to let the resolved text_id become the
photo caption instead. Two consequences: an image/video/location attachment
sets reply_markup to {} (no buttons on that message), and a caption is capped
by Telegram at ~1024 chars.
TWO REPLY-KEYBOARD BUTTON FLAGS REMOVE WHOLE DIALOG STEPS. Telegram passes
attachment.buttons straight into reply_markup.keyboard, so these survive:
{"text":"...", "request_contact":true}   -> the user taps and Telegram sends
a contact message; the receiver normalises it to
{type:"contact", contact:{name, phone}}, read as message.contact.phone
{"text":"...", "request_location":true}  -> normalised to
{type:"location", location:{lat, lon}}, read as message.location.lat/.lon
(NOTE lat/lon, not latitude/longitude)
Prefer request_contact over asking someone to type their phone number, and
keep the typed fallback in the keep node anyway: other channels have no such
button and a Telegram user can ignore it.
Each top-level key below is a SEPARATE task — do not write this file as
one task.

mainKeyboard._note: Already exists in a fresh orchestrator. Add one button per generated command; this is what makes a command discoverable.

orderStatusKeyboard._note: Enum-answer / confirm dialog step. telegram uses type:"keyboard" ON PURPOSE: a reply keyboard sends the button LABEL as a text message, which is what the wait node reads from data.message.text. An inline_keyboard here sends callback_data, which Main parses as a new COMMAND, so the pending question would never be answered. Keep the regex on the step anyway: Viber and ABC let the user type instead of tapping.

phoneKeyboard._note: Collect a phone number without anyone typing it. request_contact makes Telegram send a contact message, which the receiver normalises to {type:"contact", contact:{name, phone}} -- so the keep node reads message.contact.phone and falls back to message.text. A shared contact and a typed answer are formatted differently (a shared one usually carries the country code and a +, a typed one often does not), so normalise both to whatever form the callee's params describe before validating. Only telegram has this button; on other channels the same step is a plain typed answer, which is why the telegram key is the only one here.

locationKeyboard._note: Same idea for coordinates. The receiver normalises the reply to {type:"location", location:{lat, lon}} -- lat/lon, NOT latitude/longitude. Validate presence in the keep node (a typed reply has no location) and re-ask rather than calling the domain process with empty coordinates.

photoAttachment._note: A per-task image: url is interpolated from the CALLING task, so the command must forward that field in its Send Message api_copy data. No caption key here on purpose -- Telegram native syntax only overrides data.text when attachment.caption is set, so leaving it out lets the resolved text_id become the photo caption. Note reply_markup is {} for an image, so this message carries no buttons; send a second message if the menu must stay visible.

carouselPattern._note: Dynamic list. items is a template rendered once per element of the task's items array by createDynamicAttachment; currentPage drives paging. Ships with the wizard — reuse it before writing your own. THE CALLER MUST FORWARD items AND currentPage in its Send Message api_copy data or this renders empty; see the top comment for the items:"" vs items:[] trap.
